Forecast Discussion

High pressure sits on top of the mountains today, then slides north of us tonight. Valleys start the day with frost and warm nicely under full sun. Valleys turn chilly again tonight, though not as dramatically as this morning.

Another high builds over New England Wednesday. An easterly flow around its southern side adds clouds and takes a few degrees off the afternoon.

The easterly flow fades early Thursday, leading to a quick warmup Thursday and Friday afternoons.

The high rebuilds over New England Saturday while low pressure stays out in the Plains. Clouds thicken Saturday, but trick-or-treating stays dry. Moisture riding up and over cooler air near the surface arrives from the south overnight -- I cannot completely rule out spotty light rain late Saturday night, and light rain is possible Sunday, mostly in the afternoon. Periods of rain follow Sunday night into Monday. With the low parked to our west, the wet pattern lingers into early next week; how much rain falls is the open question.
